text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Airbus receives a 120-plane order from U.S. airline USAir, with options on a further 280 aircraft. Total price may reach up to 90 billion francs on estimates based on Airbus catalogue prices.
LES ECHOS
-- European Commission forecast based on expected economic activity for 1997, sees 12 countries qualifying to join a European single currency, calls for sustained efforts to clean up public finances.
-- Unions and town mayors call for halt of privatisation by private placement of CIC bank, a GAN subsidiary.
-- Elf Aquitaine, Murphy and Chevron to merge oil refinery and distribution in Britain.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES
-- Member of Parliament studying project to set up a parliamentary committee looking at Thomson privatisation suggests bidder Lagardere could remain in Thomson Multimedia's capital along with Daewoo.
-- Socialist party drops idea of including a legal obligation for hiring young unemployed workers in text to be debated for its social and economic party platform.
-- Framatome chairman Jean-Claude Leny to be replaced by Dominique Vignon, who favours government-backed merger project with GEC Alsthom.
L'AGEFI
-- Eiffage issues 3.5 billion francs of 280-franc convertible bonds, to reduce bank debt.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Daewoo chairman Kim Woo-choong says may set up his group's Europe headquarters in Paris if bid on Thomson Multimedia is accepted.
-- CGIP sells a 3.98 percent stake in Cap Gemini, as part of asset sales designed to finance acquisition of auto parts maker Valeo.
-- Study ranks supermarket group Carrefour top French company for adding value to its equity.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Lorry drivers to demonstrate today against effects of tax increase on fuel.
-- Thomson workers at Angers demonstrate against planned takeover by Daewoo.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Tensions over a European single currency intensify as EU predicts 12 countries will qualify on time.
-- Canal Plus planned cable-TV venture with Telefonica de Espana is likely to be blocked by EU authorities.
